security_audit.summary: Most findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, OMERO identifiers, documentation links, and safe configuration examples. Two filesystem examples have path traversal risks because server-provided filenames are joined directly to local download directories before writing. No prompt injection, concealed payload, data-exfiltration intent, or unauthorized command execution was found.

remediation.issue: Downloaded OMERO filenames are used directly as local path components.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize filenames with Path(name).name, reject separators, resolve paths, and verify every destination remains inside the intended download directory.

content.value_statement: Microscopy teams need reliable access to OMERO data and analysis workflows. This skill provides practical Python patterns for connections, images, metadata, ROIs, tables, and batch scripts.
actual_capabilities: Guide secure OMERO Python connections with credentials, sessions, group contexts, and connection cleanup.
Retrieve projects, datasets, images, screens, plates, wells, and related metadata through BlitzGateway.
Access pixel planes as NumPy arrays, configure rendering, create thumbnails, and generate derived images.
Create, retrieve, and analyze ROI shapes, including intensity measurements within selected regions.
Create annotations and OMERO tables for tags, key-value metadata, files, comments, and quantitative results.
Design OMERO server scripts and batch workflows for repeated image processing and result storage.
limitations: Requires an accessible OMERO server, valid credentials, Python, omero-py, and compatible ZeroC Ice dependencies.
Provides reference patterns, not a running connector or bundled automation service.
Examples use placeholder identifiers and must be adapted to local permissions, namespaces, and data models.
Administrative, deletion, and cross-group operations require explicit authorization and careful review before execution.

use_cases.title: Analyze screening images
use_cases.description: Retrieve plate images, inspect pixel data, measure regions, and store quantitative results in OMERO tables.

use_cases.title: Standardize OMERO workflows
use_cases.description: Create consistent connection, annotation, permission, and lifecycle patterns for shared imaging projects.

use_cases.title: Build server-side processing
use_cases.description: Design parameterized OMERO scripts for authorized batch analysis, progress reporting, cleanup, and result publication.

prompt_templates.title: Connect and list projects
prompt_templates.prompt: Show a secure Python pattern to connect to OMERO at {host} and list projects. Use environment variables and always close the session.

prompt_templates.title: Retrieve dataset images
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a workflow to retrieve images from OMERO dataset {dataset_id}. Include metadata fields, pagination, missing-object handling, and session cleanup.

prompt_templates.title: Measure ROI intensities
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an analysis for image {image_id} that retrieves ROIs, extracts channel {channel} pixels, calculates intensity statistics, and stores results in an OMERO table.

prompt_templates.title: Design an authorized batch pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an OMERO server script that processes images from {dataset_id}, stores measurements in a table, handles failures, and reports progress. Include permission checks, idempotency, and a dry-run plan.

output_examples.input: Connect to my OMERO server and summarize available projects.
output: A connection plan using protected OMERO environment variables
A project inventory with identifiers, owners, and groups
Session cleanup and connection error guidance

output_examples.input: Measure channel intensity for every rectangular ROI on an image.
output_examples.output: A workflow that retrieves rectangles, reads the selected pixel plane, computes bounded-region statistics, and prepares table rows linked to the image.

output_examples.input: Design a batch analysis script for a large dataset.
output_examples.output: A batch-script design with parameters, progress reporting, a result-table schema, permission checks, bounded processing, failure handling, and cleanup steps.

best_practices: Use environment variables or protected configuration files for credentials, and never place real passwords in prompts or generated source.
Confirm object identifiers, ownership, group context, and permissions before write, delete, or administrative operations.
Sanitize downloaded filenames, close OMERO services, and process large pixel datasets in bounded chunks or generators.
anti_patterns: Do not execute deletion, impersonation, or cross-group actions without explicit authorization and a reviewed object list.
Do not trust server-provided filenames when writing downloads to the local filesystem.
Do not load entire multidimensional image collections into memory when streaming or tiled access is available.

faq.question: Does this skill connect to OMERO directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and code patterns. The user or agent must run them with authorized network access and required dependencies.

faq.question: How should I provide OMERO credentials?
faq.answer: Use environment variables, a protected configuration file, or an approved secret manager. Never place real credentials in prompts or committed files.

faq.question: Can the generated workflows modify OMERO data?
faq.answer: Yes. Annotation, table, ROI, rendering, and deletion examples can change server data when executed with sufficient permissions.

faq.question: Does it support high-content screening data?
faq.answer: Yes. The references cover screens, plates, wells, well samples, images, and table-based measurement results.

faq.question: Does the skill install omero-py automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents an installation command, but installation and dependency management remain explicit user actions.

faq.question: Which operations need additional review?
faq.answer: Review downloads, deletions, administrator actions, user substitution, cross-group queries, and all writes against local permissions and retention policies.
